featured.title: Nepal Flood Death Toll Surges Past 330 as Glacier Collapse Scale Becomes Clear
featured.excerpt: Scientists confirm an ice-rock avalanche, not an earthquake, triggered one of Nepal's worst natural disasters, with over 900 people still missing including dozens of Americans and 177 Indian pilgrims.
featured.image_caption: An aerial view shows houses buried under mud and debris following flash floods in Nepal on August 26, 2026. The floods killed over 330 people and left more than 900 missing across eight districts.
featured.nri_angle: 177 Indian pilgrims en route to Kailash Mansarovar are among the missing, 63 Americans unaccounted for, and downstream flooding prompted evacuations in Bihar — the disaster has direct implications for diaspora families across South Asia.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

editorial.title: Who Is Anil Chakravarthy? The Bengaluru Boy Who Became a Chancellor's Gold Medalist, an MIT PhD, a Silicon Valley CEO — and Now Adobe's Next Leader
editorial.excerpt: Adobe's board has named Anil Chakravarthy as its next president and CEO, making him the second consecutive Indian-origin leader at the helm of the creative software giant. His journey from Basavanagudi to the C-suite is a story of quiet, methodical ambition.
editorial.image_caption: Anil Chakravarthy, who has been named Adobe's next CEO effective December 1, 2026, succeeding Shantanu Narayen.
editorial.nri_angle: Adobe's CEO succession from one Indian-origin leader to another underscores the growing dominance of Indian-educated executives in global tech leadership.
editorial.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Nepal Beat UAE to Win ACC Premier Cup and Book Asia Cup 2027 Spot
just_in.excerpt: Aasif Sheikh's century and Gulsan Jha's late assault powered Nepal to 313, before Karan KC and Lalit Rajbanshi derailed a UAE chase anchored by Rahul Chopra's unbeaten hundred at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur.
just_in.image_caption: Nepal's players celebrate with the trophy and a champions banner after winning the ACC Men's Premier Cup 2026 final. Nepal beat the UAE by 44 runs in Kuala Lumpur to seal qualification for the Asia Cup 2027.
just_in.nri_angle: The UAE's squad is stacked with Indian-origin players, including captain Harpreet Singh Bhatia and centurion Rahul Chopra, highlighting the diaspora's role in Gulf cricket.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Indian-Origin Surrey Landlady Arrested After Tenant's Viral Harassment Videos
just_in.excerpt: Raj Tiwana was taken into custody by Surrey Police after a tenant documented alleged harassment, unauthorized entries, and physical confrontations in videos that spread widely online. Police have issued no official statement, and the exact charges remain unclear.

just_in.title: Air India Warns of Flight Disruptions as UK Air Traffic Fault Grounds 2,000 Flights
just_in.excerpt: A technical failure at Britain's air traffic control provider NATS forced more than 1,750 flight cancellations on Tuesday, leaving over 330,000 passengers stranded. Air India advised travellers to check flight status before heading to the airport.
just_in.image_caption: Delayed passengers queue with their luggage at Heathrow airport in west London on Tuesday. More than 1,750 flights were cancelled after a technical fault at Britain’s air traffic control provider NATS disrupted operations.
just_in.nri_angle: Air India's UK routes connect London Heathrow and Birmingham with Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru — one of the busiest diaspora corridors — so the outage hits students, families and festive-season bookings directly; passengers should check flight status before heading to the airport and know their rebooking and duty-of-care rights under UK rules.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: MIT's Injectable 'Nanoantennas' Destroy Drug-Resistant Brain Cancer Cells
just_in.excerpt: The magnetically activated HITMAN technology eliminated 52 percent of chemotherapy-resistant glioblastoma cells in lab tests and extended survival in mice, without harming healthy brain tissue.
just_in.image_caption: An illustration of injectable nanoantennas being wirelessly activated by a magnetic field to target a brain tumor. MIT Media Lab researchers developed the HITMAN technology to destroy drug-resistant glioblastoma cells while leaving healthy tissue unharmed.
just_in.nri_angle: The breakthrough was led by MIT Media Lab's Deblina Sarkar, an Indian-origin researcher heading the Nano-Cybernetic Biotrek group.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Fat Cells Keep Hunger Signal Stuck 'On' After Weight Loss, Study Finds
just_in.excerpt: Case Western Reserve researchers say a lasting "obesity memory" in fat tissue may explain why weight returns after dieting or stopping GLP-1 drugs — and can pass from mother to child.
just_in.image_caption: The study’s graphical abstract shows how fat cells retain an "obesity memory" that keeps appetite high after weight loss, and how the signal passes from mother to child. The research was published in Cell Reports by scientists at Case Western Reserve University and the Harrington Discovery Institute.
just_in.nri_angle: India's growing obesity and diabetes burden makes the weight-regain problem familiar to diaspora families; the study was led by Indian-origin scientist Dr. Atul Chopra.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Harleen Deol Joins Barbados Tridents for Remainder of WCPL 2026
just_in.excerpt: The 28-year-old India batter becomes the fifth Indian in this year's Women's Caribbean Premier League, linking up with Kiran Navgire and Pooja Vastrakar for her first global franchise stint.
just_in.image_caption: Harleen Deol celebrates with the Indian flag after India’s ODI World Cup triumph in 2025. The 28-year-old batter has signed with the Barbados Tridents for the remainder of the WCPL 2026 season.
just_in.nri_angle: A fifth Indian joins the Caribbean league, with three Indians now in the defending champions' squad.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.image_caption: Anila Baby in a booking photo. The 32-year-old is charged with two counts of first-degree murder in the killings of two friends in San Jose and Milpitas, California.

just_in.title: Justice Department Sues Arkansas Over In-State Tuition for Immigrant Students
just_in.excerpt: Thursday's lawsuits against Arkansas, Hawaii, Utah and D.C. bring the administration's total to 25, as the DOJ says it has now challenged every state offering tuition breaks to noncitizens.
just_in.image_caption: The Arkansas State Capitol in Little Rock. The Justice Department has sued Arkansas, Hawaii, Utah and Washington, D.C., over laws granting in-state tuition to noncitizen students.
just_in.nri_angle: The outcome matters well beyond Arkansas: immigrant families across the 25 sued states — including Indian students and work-authorized families paying in-state rates — face the prospect of sharply higher college costs.

just_in.title: Immigration Court Waits Keep Rising Even as Deportations Hit Record Pace
just_in.excerpt: TRAC data show people ordered removed in July waited an average of 901 days — up 51% in two years — even as judges completed a record 104,028 deportation cases.
just_in.image_caption: The Bishop Henry Whipple Federal Building near Minneapolis, which houses an immigration court. The court backlog has passed 3 million cases, with backlogged cases waiting an average of 940 days, according to TRAC.
just_in.nri_angle: For immigrants of all nationalities navigating the U.S. system, the data point to longer years of legal limbo even as the machinery of removal runs faster than ever.

just_in.title: Telangana Bans Artificial Non-Dairy Paneer for One Year After Raids
just_in.excerpt: The state's food safety authority prohibited analogue paneer sold as "paneer" from September 10, 2026, and suspended five FSSAI licences in Hyderabad after enforcement drives found unhygienic conditions and adulterated ingredients.
just_in.image_caption: Seized bags labelled cheese analogue are piled up during a food safety enforcement drive in Telangana. The state has banned the manufacture and sale of non-dairy analogue paneer sold as paneer for one year from September 10, 2026.
just_in.nri_angle: Diaspora shoppers are reminded to check paneer ingredient labels abroad — genuine paneer lists milk and an acidulant, while substitutes rely on vegetable oils and emulsifiers — and families visiting Telangana will find restaurant paneer under closer scrutiny.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Global Funds Lose Faith in India as Some Cut Stock Allocations to Zero
just_in.excerpt: Money managers at Janus Henderson and Vantage Point have pared India exposure to zero, and foreign portfolio ownership has tumbled to a 17-year low as AI-rich North Asia steals the flows.
just_in.image_caption: An illustration shows hands pulling apart the pieces of a red pie chart. Global funds have pulled a net $25 billion from Indian stocks this year, with foreign portfolio ownership of NSE-listed companies falling to a 17-year low.
just_in.nri_angle: India raised $127 billion from its diaspora to defend the rupee, showing how directly overseas Indians are being pulled into the country's currency battle — and NRI portfolios tied to Indian equities are feeling the foreign exodus first-hand.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Afghanistan vs India T20Is: Full Schedule, Squads and How to Watch
just_in.excerpt: Three T20 internationals at Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 13, 15 and 17 — Afghanistan's first series as host against India, with Jasprit Bumrah back in India's squad.
just_in.image_caption: India players gather in a huddle during a T20I match, wearing the team blue kit sponsored by Apollo Tyres. India face Afghanistan in a three-match T20I series at Delhis Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 13, 15 and 17, 2026.
just_in.nri_angle: The series sits at the intersection of two of cricket's most followed fan bases — the Indian and Afghan diasporas in the UK, North America and the Gulf — with morning start times in North America making the games easy to follow live.

just_in.title: TSMC Posts Record August Revenue as AI Boom Keeps Foundries Fully Booked
just_in.excerpt: Taiwan Semiconductor posted NT$514.8 billion in August sales — up 53% from a year ago — but investors barely blinked, with the stock slipping as the AI trade shows signs of fatigue.
just_in.image_caption: TSMC chairman C.C. Wei. TSMC posted record August revenue of NT$514.8 billion, up 53.3% from a year earlier, as AI chip demand kept its advanced foundries fully booked.
just_in.nri_angle: TSMC anchors most semiconductor and emerging-market index funds held by global investors, so its guidance and pricing power shape portfolios well beyond Taiwan.

news.nri_angle: For NRIs with property and family ties in India, a common code governing inheritance and succession across states could simplify estate matters, though the rollout is several years out.

news.title: Pakistan rules out immediate military action under Mecca pact after Houthi attacks
news.excerpt: Islamabad says no military response is under discussion following Houthi strikes on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure, but pledges it will act under the trilateral defence pact 'when time comes.'
news.image_caption: The Great Mosque of Mecca. Pakistan says no military response is currently being discussed under the Mecca defence pact it signed with Turkey and Saudi Arabia.
news.nri_angle: Millions of Indians live and work in Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf; any widening of the conflict threatens their safety and remittance flows, while crude price spikes feed India's import bill.

news.title: Rights groups condemn 'racist murder' of Manipuri singer in Delhi, demand racial-motive probe
news.excerpt: Civil society and human rights organisations say the mob killing of musician Chongtham Vikram Singh must be examined in the wider context of racial violence against people from Northeast India.
news.image_caption: A candle-lighting vigil for Chongtham Vikram, the 55-year-old Manipuri guitarist killed in Delhi. Rights groups have condemned his murder as racially motivated.
news.nri_angle: For the Northeastern diaspora abroad, the case is a measure of how India confronts racial violence at home, shaping how safe the community feels in Indian cities.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Condemns Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia as 'Unacceptable' Threat to Region
news.excerpt: New Delhi denounced Houthi strikes on Saudi civilian and economic sites that injured 73 people, warning the escalation threatens regional stability and freedom of navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb.
news.image_caption: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal speaks at a press briefing in New Delhi. India condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's civilian and economic infrastructure, which injured 73 people, as unacceptable.
news.nri_angle: Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian expatriate communities in the world, and attacks on its oil infrastructure feed directly into crude prices that shape inflation in India.

news.title: Lancet Study: Passive Smoking Deaths in India Jump 50% Since 1990
news.excerpt: Deaths from second-hand smoke in India rose from about 217,700 to 325,600 between 1990 and 2023, with 444 million Indians now exposed — the world's second-highest total after China.
news.image_caption: A smoker exhales a cloud of cigarette smoke. A Lancet study finds passive-smoking deaths in India have jumped 50 percent since 1990.
news.nri_angle: The findings matter for Indian-American multi-generational households, where grandparents visiting from India may smoke indoors and children face the greatest health burden from second-hand exposure.

nri-world.excerpt: ReuniteIndia.com consolidates scattered official records into a single searchable database of people missing in the Nepal floods, with QR-coded live case pages.

nri-world.title: Stalker Kills Sacramento Woman Despite Restraining Order; Mother Blames System

nri-world.image_caption: Downtown Sacramento. A woman was killed by a stalker despite a restraining order, prompting questions about enforcement gaps.
nri-world.nri_angle: An Indian-origin woman working a service job in California was killed by her alleged stalker despite a restraining order, raising urgent safety questions for immigrant workers in the diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Kerala Crash Kills NRI Family of Three; 36-Hour Arrest Delay Raises Questions
nri-world.excerpt: The deaths of Gulf returnee Muneer, his wife and their 3-year-old son have revived questions about delayed alcohol evidence — echoing the 2019 Venkitaraman case.

nri-world.nri_angle: Muneer was a Gulf returnee — his death resonates across Kerala's diaspora, where nearly every family has someone working abroad.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: "Talent Is Universal, Opportunity Is Not": Wadhwani Foundation CEO Dr. Ajay Kela on Why the Diaspora's Greatest Asset Isn't Money
nri-world.excerpt: In an exclusive interview with The Videshi, the CEO of Wadhwani Foundation talks about India's innovation ecosystem, the "missing middle" of Indian entrepreneurship, and why the diaspora's most powerful currency isn't capital — it's knowledge.
nri-world.image_caption: Dr. Ajay Kela, CEO and Board Member of Wadhwani Foundation, leads the organization's mission to create 5 million jobs and upskill 25 million people across emerging economies.
nri-world.nri_angle: Interview with Dr. Ajay Kela, NRI leader who returned to India to lead Wadhwani Foundation — covers diaspora giving back, deep-tech opportunities, and India's innovation ecosystem.

immigration.title: 'Do We Want to Deport Foreign Doctors?' CEO Challenges H-1B Grace-Period Repeal
immigration.excerpt: Seattle immigration-firm CEO Xiao Wang says a Department of Homeland Security proposal to scrap the 60-day grace period for laid-off H-1B workers would force foreign doctors and engineers out of the country immediately — even when another employer wants to hire them.
immigration.nri_angle: Indians form the largest share of H-1B holders and the deepest green-card backlog among foreign physicians, so a rule converting any layoff into an immediate departure order would fall hardest on Indian doctors and the safety-net hospitals that depend on them.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Justice Department Sues Arkansas Over In-State Tuition for Immigrant Students
immigration.excerpt: Thursday's lawsuits against Arkansas, Hawaii, Utah and D.C. bring the administration's total to 25, as the DOJ says it has now challenged every state offering tuition breaks to noncitizens.
immigration.image_caption: The Arkansas State Capitol in Little Rock. The Justice Department has sued Arkansas, Hawaii, Utah and Washington, D.C., over laws granting in-state tuition to noncitizen students.
immigration.nri_angle: The outcome matters well beyond Arkansas: immigrant families across the 25 sued states — including Indian students and work-authorized families paying in-state rates — face the prospect of sharply higher college costs.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Immigration Court Waits Keep Rising Even as Deportations Hit Record Pace
immigration.excerpt: TRAC data show people ordered removed in July waited an average of 901 days — up 51% in two years — even as judges completed a record 104,028 deportation cases.
immigration.image_caption: The Bishop Henry Whipple Federal Building near Minneapolis, which houses an immigration court. The court backlog has passed 3 million cases, with backlogged cases waiting an average of 940 days, according to TRAC.
immigration.nri_angle: For immigrants of all nationalities navigating the U.S. system, the data point to longer years of legal limbo even as the machinery of removal runs faster than ever.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: ACLU Sues Hartford Immigration Court Over Withheld Basic Case Records
immigration.excerpt: The Connecticut ACLU chapter filed a federal lawsuit this week against the U.S. attorney general and Hartford's chief immigration judge, arguing the public has a First Amendment right to docket numbers, case captions, and in absentia removal orders without waiting months for a FOIA response.
immigration.image_caption: The Abraham A. Ribicoff Federal Building in Hartford, Connecticut, which houses the Hartford immigration court. The ACLU has sued the court over withheld basic case records.
immigration.nri_angle: Indian immigrants navigating asylum or removal proceedings in Connecticut depend on public scrutiny of immigration courts to ensure their cases receive fair process.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: El Salvador TPS Holds Past Its Deadline as Employers Await DHS Guidance
immigration.excerpt: The designation's September 9 expiry passed with no Federal Register notice from DHS, leaving beneficiaries protected but employers without updated I-9 instructions.
immigration.image_caption: The national flag of El Salvador. DHS has not issued a termination or extension notice for the TPS designation, leaving employers without updated Form I-9 guidance.
immigration.nri_angle: Immigration-watch readers — including employers of TPS workers and diaspora members tracking DHS policy shifts — need to know what remains in effect and where the documentation gap lies.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Indian man jailed 27 years in Australia for fatal stabbing, faces deportation
immigration.excerpt: Robin Robin, 30, was sentenced in the Victorian Supreme Court for murdering 22-year-old Navjeet Singh Sandhu and attempting to murder Sharwan Singh during a drunken rampage in Ormond in May 2024. He will not be eligible for parole for 20 years and is expected to be deported to India.
immigration.image_caption: Melbourne, where the Victorian Supreme Court sentenced Robin Robin to 27 years in prison for a fatal stabbing in Ormond.
immigration.nri_angle: The sentencing shows how a serious criminal conviction in Australia leads to visa cancellation and post-sentence deportation for Indian nationals, a direct warning for the large Indian student and migrant community.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: DHS Proposes $103,265 Fee on Every H-1B Cap Petition in Sweeping Rulemaking
immigration.excerpt: DHS says the fee would recover $8.8 billion a year in federal immigration costs. Unlike the struck-down $100,000 order, it would apply even to F-1 students changing status inside the U.S.
immigration.image_caption: The U.S. Capitol in Washington. The Department of Homeland Security has proposed a $103,265 fee on every H-1B cap petition.
immigration.nri_angle: Indian nationals receive the largest share of H-1B visas, so a six-figure fee would sharply raise employer costs for hiring Indian tech workers and could cool H-1B demand.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: September Visa Bulletin Brings Biggest Family Green Card Advances in Years
immigration.excerpt: Family-sponsored final action dates jumped by up to 29 months, with India gaining in F2B and F3 — but employment-based categories froze and India EB-2 stays unavailable.
immigration.image_caption: Immigration paperwork, including an Affidavit of Support form, an IRS account transcript, and a calculator on a desk. The State Department's September 2026 Visa Bulletin brought some of the largest forward movements in recent years across family-sponsored green card categories.
immigration.nri_angle: Indian family-sponsored applicants gain years of forward movement in F2B and F3, while Indian professionals in employment-based lines see no relief and face possible retrogression before October.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: DOL Suspends New PERM Green Card Filings by Cognizant, Cloudera
immigration.excerpt: The Labor Department's inspector general froze new permanent labor certification filings at the two tech firms amid a fraud probe — stalling green card sponsorships for thousands of H-1B workers, with no charges yet announced.
immigration.image_caption: TR Immigration social card image accompanying its report on the PERM filing suspensions. The Labor Department inspector general announced on September 8, 2026 that new permanent labor certification filings by Cognizant and Cloudera were frozen during a fraud investigation.
immigration.nri_angle: The freeze stalls green card sponsorships for thousands of Indian H-1B professionals at Cognizant and Cloudera, including the six-year extensions that depend on pending PERM or approved I-140 petitions.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Newly Discovered Canadian Citizenship: How to Sponsor Your Spouse for Permanent Residence
immigration.excerpt: Citizenship by descent follows bloodlines, not marriage — but as a Canadian citizen you can sponsor your spouse or partner for PR, leading eventually to citizenship.
immigration.image_caption: A couple reviews immigration paperwork at home, a Canadian flag on the wall. New guidance clarifies how newly discovered Canadian citizens can sponsor a spouse for permanent residence.
immigration.nri_angle: Many Indian-origin US families discover Canadian citizenship through a parent or grandparent, and spousal sponsorship can reshape their whole immigration strategy amid tightening US visa rules.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Indian Creator's Schengen Visa Rejected: The 3 Mistakes She Wants You to Avoid
immigration.excerpt: Garima Singh's rejection notice cited an unreliable itinerary, an uncertain purpose of stay and a name mismatch — three classic red flags behind India's 181,000 Schengen refusals last year.
immigration.image_caption: An open passport covered in visa stamps and entry markings. The image reflects the documentation pitfalls flagged by an Indian creator whose Schengen visa application was rejected.
immigration.nri_angle: Practical service journalism for Indian travellers planning Europe trips — and a cautionary tale for NRIs hosting family visits to the Schengen zone.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: 170,000 Salvadorans Face Uncertain Future as Trump Targets Their Protected Status
immigration.excerpt: Their Temporary Protected Status was set to expire September 9, but DHS has not announced a decision — leaving a community that has lived legally in the US for 25 years in limbo.
immigration.image_caption: A woman speaks during an interview at her home, where packed boxes are visible. Around 170,000 Salvadoran TPS holders are awaiting a Department of Homeland Security decision on their protections.
immigration.nri_angle: Indians are not a major TPS group, but the pattern matters: the administration is systematically dismantling humanitarian protections, and diaspora communities are watching how courts and Congress respond.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: NSE Leads Rs 24,600 Crore IPO Bonanza With 11 Issues Opening Next Week
markets-finance.excerpt: Eleven IPOs targeting a combined Rs 24,574 crore open for subscription next week, headlined by the NSE's long-awaited Rs 22,569 crore listing — India's second-largest public issue ever — alongside a Rs 1,000 crore Hero Motors offering.
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI and OCI investors can participate in Indian IPOs through NRE/NRO accounts under FEMA rules, so the year's headline offerings — including the NSE listing — are directly accessible to the diaspora.

markets-finance.title: India Overtakes Russia as Fourth-Largest Forex Reserve Holder After Record $44.9B Surge
markets-finance.excerpt: The RBI said reserves jumped a record $44.9 billion to a lifetime high of $785.7 billion in the week ended September 4, driven by the central bank's FCNR(B) deposit scheme — with a Rs 1 lakh crore bond sale now planned to mop up excess liquidity.
markets-finance.nri_angle: A record forex stockpile strengthens the rupee's floor against global shocks, which directly affects exchange rates for remittances and the returns of India-linked portfolios.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Global Funds Lose Faith in India as Some Cut Stock Allocations to Zero
markets-finance.excerpt: Money managers at Janus Henderson and Vantage Point have pared India exposure to zero, and foreign portfolio ownership has tumbled to a 17-year low as AI-rich North Asia steals the flows.

markets-finance.nri_angle: India raised $127 billion from its diaspora to defend the rupee, showing how directly overseas Indians are being pulled into the country's currency battle — and NRI portfolios tied to Indian equities are feeling the foreign exodus first-hand.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: TSMC Posts Record August Revenue as AI Boom Keeps Foundries Fully Booked
markets-finance.excerpt: Taiwan Semiconductor posted NT$514.8 billion in August sales — up 53% from a year ago — but investors barely blinked, with the stock slipping as the AI trade shows signs of fatigue.
markets-finance.image_caption: TSMC chairman C.C. Wei. TSMC posted record August revenue of NT$514.8 billion, up 53.3% from a year earlier, as AI chip demand kept its advanced foundries fully booked.
markets-finance.nri_angle: TSMC anchors most semiconductor and emerging-market index funds held by global investors, so its guidance and pricing power shape portfolios well beyond Taiwan.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: US Consumer Sentiment Plunges in September as Inflation Fears Mount
markets-finance.excerpt: The University of Michigan's sentiment index fell to 47.8 in early September while year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 4.6%, the highest since June.
markets-finance.image_caption: Shoppers at a supermarket. The University of Michigan's Consumer Sentiment Index fell to 47.8 in early September as inflation expectations jumped.
markets-finance.nri_angle: With sentiment near historic lows and inflation expectations rising, diaspora households should factor weaker hiring prospects and persistent grocery and fuel costs into fall spending and home-buying decisions.

markets-finance.title: EPF Withdrawal Rules: What EPFO's Simplified Advance Norms Mean for Your Savings

markets-finance.title: Adyen to Expand India Operations as Local Profits More Than Double
markets-finance.excerpt: The Dutch payments processor is betting on India's digital payments growth and rising cross-border commerce, with local headcount up tenfold since 2023 and pre-tax income at €3.18 million.

sports.title: Rajeev Ram Retires After US Open Semifinal Loss, Ending Storied Doubles Career
sports.excerpt: The former world No. 1 doubles star played his final match alongside Joe Salisbury on September 11, then gave a tearful on-court farewell honoring his late father.
sports.image_caption: Rajeev Ram receives a commemorative frame during his on-court farewell ceremony at the US Open. The former doubles world No. 1 retired after playing his final match on September 11, 2026.
sports.nri_angle: The greatest Indian-American tennis player of all time says goodbye at the tournament where he built his legacy.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Afghanistan vs India T20Is: Full Schedule, Squads and How to Watch
sports.excerpt: Three T20 internationals at Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 13, 15 and 17 — Afghanistan's first series as host against India, with Jasprit Bumrah back in India's squad.
sports.image_caption: India players gather in a huddle during a T20I match, wearing the team blue kit sponsored by Apollo Tyres. India face Afghanistan in a three-match T20I series at Delhis Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 13, 15 and 17, 2026.
sports.nri_angle: The series sits at the intersection of two of cricket's most followed fan bases — the Indian and Afghan diasporas in the UK, North America and the Gulf — with morning start times in North America making the games easy to follow live.

sports.title: Babar Azam Enters Record Books With 2,000 WTC Runs as Captain
sports.excerpt: The Pakistan captain's 76 at Edgbaston made him the fourth batter — and second Asian — to reach 2,000 World Test Championship runs as captain, a milestone that eluded India's Kohli and Rohit. But England completed a 3-0 whitewash.
sports.image_caption: Babar Azam. The former Pakistan captain became only the fourth captain to score 2,000 runs in the World Test Championship, reaching the milestone at Edgbaston.
sports.nri_angle: A record that eluded Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma as captains gives subcontinent cricket fans — including millions in the diaspora — a fresh statistical lens on Babar Azam's standing, even as Pakistan's tour ended in a 3-0 whitewash.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Bumrah Finds Rhythm in Delhi Nets Ahead of Afghanistan T20I Return
sports.excerpt: Bowling at full intensity in Thursday's Delhi nets, Jasprit Bumrah looked ready for his first T20I since March. Shreyas Iyer wants him to get game time; Afghanistan say they have a plan for him.
sports.image_caption: Jasprit Bumrah. The pacer bowled at full intensity in the Delhi nets on Thursday as he closes in on a T20I return against Afghanistan.

sports.title: Anmol Ekka Double Fires India Into Fourth Straight Junior Asia Cup Final
sports.excerpt: India beat Malaysia 3-1 in Moqi, China, with captain Ekka scoring twice and goalkeeper Vivek Lakra saving a penalty stroke; South Korea await in Sunday's final.

sports.title: India's New Zealand Tour Sells 50,000 Tickets in Two Weeks
sports.excerpt: NZ Cricket sold more than 50,000 tickets in just over two weeks for India's first tour in six years, reopening Eden Park's sixth tier for the first time since 2019.
sports.image_caption: A packed cricket stadium under lights during a night match. Tickets for India's tour of New Zealand sold 50,000 seats within two weeks.
sports.nri_angle: India fixtures draw the largest and loudest diaspora crowds of any touring side in New Zealand, home to one of the world's fastest-growing Indian communities.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: MIT's Injectable 'Nanoantennas' Destroy Drug-Resistant Brain Cancer Cells
technology.excerpt: The magnetically activated HITMAN technology eliminated 52 percent of chemotherapy-resistant glioblastoma cells in lab tests and extended survival in mice, without harming healthy brain tissue.
technology.image_caption: An illustration of injectable nanoantennas being wirelessly activated by a magnetic field to target a brain tumor. MIT Media Lab researchers developed the HITMAN technology to destroy drug-resistant glioblastoma cells while leaving healthy tissue unharmed.
technology.nri_angle: The breakthrough was led by MIT Media Lab's Deblina Sarkar, an Indian-origin researcher heading the Nano-Cybernetic Biotrek group.

technology.title: After Anthropic Researcher's Extinction Warning, Congress Demands AI Safeguards
technology.excerpt: More than 20 members of Congress called for federal AI regulation this week after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's viral resignation warning, with Rep. Lori Trahan declaring bipartisan momentum has hit “a tipping point.”
technology.image_caption: The U.S. Capitol in Washington. More than 20 members of Congress have called for stronger AI regulation after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon quit, warning the industry is ‘gambling with our lives.’
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers make up a significant share of the U.S. AI workforce, so any federal regime of testing mandates, development pauses, or a new AI safety agency would land directly on the labs that employ them.

technology.title: Trezor Brevo Breach Exposed 347,000 Emails to Phishing Attack
technology.excerpt: A flaw in email provider Brevo's login system let attackers send phishing emails from Trezor's own domain to 347,000 newsletter subscribers — the hardware wallet maker's second third-party data breach in weeks.
technology.nri_angle: Crypto ownership runs deep in the Indian diaspora, so wallet-holding readers should scrutinize vendor-branded emails and warn family members about the phishing campaign.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: The AI 'Doomsday' Debate Moves From Silicon Valley to Mainstream America
technology.excerpt: A departing Anthropic researcher's warning about civilization-ending AI has triggered the week's biggest tech story — and new calls in Congress for guardrails.
technology.image_caption: A data center housing AI infrastructure. The debate over catastrophic AI risk has moved from Silicon Valley circles into mainstream American discourse.
technology.nri_angle: Indian engineers form a large share of the AI research workforce, so both a regulatory crackdown and unchecked deployment would land directly on diaspora careers.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: TCS Opens India's First Lights-Out Factory Lab in Pune for AI Manufacturing

technology.nri_angle: The lab advances India's positioning in AI-led manufacturing, a sector diaspora investors and tech professionals watch as a signal of where global industrial AI work is heading.

technology.title: Jio Payment Solutions Launches Cross-Border Platform for Indian Exporters

technology.nri_angle: Diaspora entrepreneurs and freelance professionals doing business with India gain a regulated, lower-friction rail for getting paid across borders.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Anthropic Researcher Quits, Says AI Labs Are 'Gambling With Our Lives'

technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Launches UPI Tap-and-Pay Ahead of Full Apple Pay Rollout

technology.title: Nilekani: Tokenisation's Time Has Come — And India Needs Public Chains

entertainment.image_caption: Keerthy Suresh poses on the red carpet at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival in a burgundy and antique-gold contemporary Kanjivaram-inspired ensemble. She attended the world premiere of her Tamil film Dorothy, directed by Karthik Subbaraj, which earned a standing ovation at the festival.
entertainment.nri_angle: Toronto is home to one of North America's largest South Asian communities, and the Dorothy premiere gives diaspora audiences an early festival encounter with a Tamil film before its September 25 theatrical release.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: AR Rahman Pitches Kashmir as Global Cinema Hub, Urges Bollywood to Film There
entertainment.excerpt: The Oscar-winning composer told ANI in Srinagar that Bollywood should project Kashmir's beauty and peace rather than its troubled past, praising the International Film Festival of Jammu and Kashmir as a launchpad for global recognition.
entertainment.image_caption: AR Rahman speaks to media personnel holding microphones in Srinagar. The Oscar-winning composer urged Bollywood to film more in Kashmir and praised the International Film Festival of Jammu and Kashmir as a commendable initiative.
entertainment.nri_angle: For the diaspora, Kashmir is one of the most emotionally resonant destinations in the subcontinent, and a Bollywood revival in the Valley championed by Rahman gives that longing a contemporary soundtrack.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Dorothy and Termite: Oscar Breakouts Chart New Course for Indian Cinema at TIFF
entertainment.excerpt: Oscar-winner Guneet Monga Kapoor premiered the Tamil gangster western “Dorothy” to a standing ovation at TIFF 2026 — her first project under Jio Studios' majority stake — while documentarian Shaunak Sen unveiled his fiction debut “Termite.”
entertainment.image_caption: Two men walk through a narrow rural street lined with old stone houses in a still from the Tamil-language film Dorothy. The Karthik Subbaraj-directed film premiered to a standing ovation at the Toronto International Film Festival this week.
entertainment.nri_angle: TIFF sits in a city with one of the world's largest South Asian diasporas, and a Tamil-language premiere backed by studio money tests whether festival prestige for Indian independent cinema can convert into diaspora box office worldwide.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Mirzapur The Movie Crosses $2 Million In North America, Climbing Indian Box Office Charts
entertainment.excerpt: The crime thriller took ₹9.5 crore on its second Friday to reach ₹163.27 crore net in India, overtaking Awarapan 2 for the year's No. 6 spot, while its $2.05 million North American haul made it the fourth Bollywood film of 2026 to cross $2 million in the territory.
entertainment.nri_angle: Mirzapur The Movie's $2.05 million North American first week — Bollywood's fourth $2M grosser of 2026 — shows how diaspora demand for established Indian series IPs converts directly into overseas box office.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Sardar 2 opens at Rs 5.30 crore, loses domestic battle to Soori's Mandaadi
entertainment.excerpt: Karthi's Sardar 2 grossed Rs 5.30 crore in India on opening day but was out-earned at home by the much smaller Soori-starrer Mandaadi, which managed Rs 5.55 crore on nearly 1,000 fewer shows. Overseas business gave the sequel a narrow worldwide lead.
entertainment.image_caption: Karthi, who stars in Sardar 2. The film opened at Rs 5.30 crore domestically, trailing Soori's Mandaadi in its first week.
entertainment.nri_angle: Overseas business was the one front where Sardar 2 led on day one, with Tamil diaspora audiences in the Gulf, Malaysia and Singapore turning out for Karthi's sequel.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Toxic week 2: Yash's film crawls to Rs 263 crore as 300-crore flop looms
entertainment.excerpt: Yash's Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups added just Rs 6.75 crore in its second weekend, taking its 12-day India gross to Rs 263 crore. Trade trackers say the costly film is headed for one of the biggest losses in Indian cinema.
entertainment.image_caption: A still from Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups, showing Yash and Kiara Advani. The Geethu Mohandas-directed film reached Rs 263 crore gross in India after 12 days and is expected to finish its run under Rs 270 crore.
entertainment.nri_angle: The film's English version, aimed partly at overseas multiplex audiences, was pulled after a week, and the theatrical collapse leaves the digital premiere as diaspora viewers' main route to the film.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Don't Be Shy trailer drops: Alia Bhatt's coming-of-age rom-com bets on fresh faces
entertainment.excerpt: The first trailer for Prime Video's Don't Be Shy introduces four debutant leads headed by Aarushi Bajaj, as producers Alia Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt back a young-adult story of first love, friendship and messy choices ahead of its September 25 premiere.
entertainment.image_caption: A collage of the four young leads of Don't Be Shy alongside producers Alia Bhatt and Shaheen Bhatt. The coming-of-age romantic comedy premieres on Prime Video on September 25, 2026.
entertainment.nri_angle: The September 25 day-and-date Prime Video release across 240+ countries brings the film to diaspora living rooms worldwide at the same time as India.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: From Mardaani to Delhi Crime: Hindi Cinema's Women Cops Take Charge
entertainment.excerpt: Rani Mukerji's franchise completed an unprecedented hattrick of hits, while streaming turned Shefali Shah, Sonakshi Sinha and Raveena Tandon into television's most compelling investigators.
entertainment.image_caption: Actor Rani Mukerji, whose Shivani Shivaji Roy in the Mardaani franchise is Hindi cinema's defining woman cop. Mardaani 3 closed its 2026 theatrical run at about Rs 77 crore, the series' best.
entertainment.nri_angle: Streaming made these performances global by default — Delhi Crime topped charts in 10 countries, giving NRI audiences a second front of Indian storytelling beyond Bollywood tentpoles.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Swara Bhasker on Bollywood's Evolution: The Khans, OTT and the Industry's Reckoning
entertainment.excerpt: In a series of candid interviews, the actor weighs in on Salman Khan's mentorship, streaming's levelling of stardom, the boycott-era slump and the industry's storytelling habits.
entertainment.image_caption: Actor Swara Bhasker. In a new interview she reflects on Bollywood's evolution, the Khans' three-decade dominance and the streaming era's reshaping of stardom.
entertainment.nri_angle: Diaspora audiences now watch Hindi cinema primarily on streaming, making Bhasker's argument that OTT has 'democratised stardom' a direct description of how NRIs experience Bollywood.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Hollywood and Regional Hits Squeeze Bollywood's Share Below 40 Percent in 2026
entertainment.excerpt: India's box office is headed for a record year, but Ormax data shows Hindi cinema ceding ground to a ₹500-crore Spider-Man and surging Telugu and Tamil releases.
entertainment.image_caption: Shenoy's Theatre in Kochi, Kerala. India's domestic box office grew 13 percent through July 2026, but Hindi cinema's share has slipped below 40 percent for the first time.
entertainment.nri_angle: Diaspora moviegoers mirror the shift, filling overseas multiplexes for Spider-Man and Telugu/Tamil blockbusters that now share screens once dominated by Hindi tentpoles.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Sharat Saxena, 76, Shares Standing MRI Photos Ahead of Lumbar Spine Surgery
entertainment.excerpt: The veteran Bollywood actor, last seen in Son of Sardaar 2, posted pictures from Mumbai's Bombay Hospital and told fans he hopes to walk properly and work again.
entertainment.image_caption: Sharat Saxena at a film event. Saxena has shared photos of his standing MRI scan ahead of lumbar spine surgery.
entertainment.nri_angle: Saxena's films from Mr. India to Baghban remain staples in NRI households, making his health update one diaspora families follow closely.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Could Your Daily Coffee Habit Actually Slow Down Aging?
lifestyle-health.excerpt: From protective brain receptors to large-scale mortality studies, researchers find moderate coffee drinking is linked with healthier aging — but the evidence comes with important caveats.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: India's diaspora is swapping filter kaapi for espresso culture — the research's two-to-three-cup sweet spot, with decaf as a viable option, fits both traditions.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Ozempic and Wegovy May Carry a Hair-Loss Risk for Some Men
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new NYU Langone study finds the first genetic link between GLP-1 drugs and male-pattern hair loss — but researchers stress the evidence is early and applies only to men already genetically predisposed.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: GLP-1 medications are widely used by Indian-American patients managing diabetes and obesity; those noticing unusual shedding should raise it with their doctor rather than abandoning a treatment whose metabolic benefits are well established.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Third of Americans May Have Fatty Liver Disease — Diet Is the Fix
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Up to 42% of American adults may have fat building up in their livers without knowing it. Doctors say the fix isn't a cleanse — it's what you eat every day.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For Indian-American households, where rich festive foods and sedentary workdays are common — and where metabolic disease strikes at lower body weights — the hepatologists' dietary advice is directly relevant family-health guidance.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Fat Cells Keep Hunger Signal Stuck 'On' After Weight Loss, Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Case Western Reserve researchers say a lasting "obesity memory" in fat tissue may explain why weight returns after dieting or stopping GLP-1 drugs — and can pass from mother to child.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: The study’s graphical abstract shows how fat cells retain an "obesity memory" that keeps appetite high after weight loss, and how the signal passes from mother to child. The research was published in Cell Reports by scientists at Case Western Reserve University and the Harrington Discovery Institute.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: India's growing obesity and diabetes burden makes the weight-regain problem familiar to diaspora families; the study was led by Indian-origin scientist Dr. Atul Chopra.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Cardiologist Urges Earlier ECG Screening for At-Risk Patients as India's Heart Disease Burden Grows
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Dr. Vijay D'Silva says skipping early ECG screening costs lives — but U.S. guidelines add an important caveat: screening pays off for at-risk patients, not healthy low-risk adults.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An illustration shows a human heart with blood vessels over an electrocardiogram waveform. Dr. Vijay D'Silva argues early ECG screening can catch silent heart disease before symptoms appear.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians develop coronary artery disease at younger ages, so the diaspora with family history of early heart disease should raise ECG screening at their annual physical.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Daily Walk Alone Won't Build Fitness: Intensity, Variety, Strength Training Matter
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Fitness expert Sumit Dubey says most walkers stall because comfortable-pace strolls never push the heart and lungs — faster intervals, varied routes, and strength work close the gap.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A group of women power walking outdoors. Fitness expert Sumit Dubey says intensity — walking fast enough to talk but not sing — matters more than duration for cardiovascular fitness.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For NRIs rooted in walking culture, the coach's advice translates to layering intensity bursts and two weekly resistance sessions onto the familiar daily walk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Cardiologist's Three Longevity Habits: Lp(a) Test, Strength Training, Treated Sleep Apnea
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Interventional cardiologist Dr. Sanjay Bhojraj says three underused steps — a one-time Lp(a) blood test, training for functional strength, and treating sleep apnea — can meaningfully slow how fast your heart ages.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A seated cable row exercise. Cardiologist Dr. Sanjay Bhojraj lists strength training among his three longevity habits, alongside an Lp(a) test and treating sleep apnea.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry elevated lipoprotein(a) more often than many populations, making the once-in-a-lifetime Lp(a) test the 2026 ACC/AHA guideline now recommends especially relevant for the Indian diaspora.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Drooping smile, weak arms: neurologists flag stroke warning signs in young adults
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A drooping smile, a weak arm and slurred speech are the classic red flags — and with four in ten Indian stroke patients now under 50, neurologists say young adults should learn the BEFAST checklist and act within the golden hours.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Brain scans. Neurologists warn that a drooping smile, weak arms, and slurred speech can signal a stroke.

sources.label: Passionate in Marketing / World Stroke Day

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians develop cardiovascular risk factors earlier and at higher rates, making BEFAST stroke awareness especially relevant in NRI households — and for spotting warning signs in ageing parents back home.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Inside Krystle D'Souza's Mumbai Home: Parisian Chic, a Glam Room and Sabyasachi Walls
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The Traitors season 2 winner gave Farah Khan a tour of her self-designed Lokhandwala apartment — from a ₹35,000-a-roll Sabyasachi bedroom wall to a bedroom-sized vanity room.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Television actor Krystle D'Souza. A new feature tours her Mumbai home, from its Parisian-chic interiors to a glam room and Sabyasachi-clad walls.

gallery_images.caption: The dining and living areas of Krystle D'Souza's Lokhandwala apartment, with beige tones, wooden textures and fluted panelling. Photo: Hindustan Times.
Farah Khan with Krystle D'Souza and her cook Dilip inside the Mumbai apartment during the September 7 home-tour vlog. Photo: Farah Khan/YouTube.

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For design-minded NRIs, the tour offers a template — Parisian detailing, Sabyasachi accents and a dedicated vanity space that translate well to diaspora homes.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Paying Extra for A2 Ghee? Cardiologist Says the Label Is a Fad
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Dr. Darshan Banker and the IFBA's Deepak Jolly say the A1/A2 protein distinction is irrelevant in ghee, which is 99.9% fat — portion size and verified purity matter far more.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A bowl of homemade ghee in Maharashtra. A cardiologist says the premium A2 ghee label is more marketing fad than medicine.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: A2 ghee sells at double or triple the price in diaspora grocery stores on imported health claims that these experts say don't survive scrutiny.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: How PCOS, Obesity and Insulin Resistance Lock Women in a Vicious Cycle
lifestyle-health.excerpt: About two-thirds of women with PCOS have insulin resistance — and each side of the triangle intensifies the other two. Doctors say treating the condition as a metabolic disorder, not just a fertility problem, is the way out.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: PCOS runs high among Indian women and the diaspora, and South Asians develop insulin resistance at lower body weights, making early metabolic screening — not just fertility treatment — especially urgent.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: DNA Hairpin Treatment Cuts Bad Cholesterol Nearly 50% Without Statins
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Scientists in Spain and the United States built short DNA molecules that switch off a cholesterol-regulating gene, cutting blood cholesterol 47% in mice after a single injection — with none of the side effects linked to statins.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A researcher at the National Human Genome Research Institute pipettes DNA from a micro test tube. Scientists used DNA-based polypurine hairpins to block production of the PCSK9 protein, cutting LDL cholesterol nearly 50% in a new study.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face disproportionately high rates of premature heart disease, so a cheaper, non-statin cholesterol treatment could matter greatly for the diaspora if it survives clinical testing.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Table for One: Are Indian Restaurants Ready for the Solo Diner?
food.excerpt: A quiet cultural shift is emptying the stigma from eating alone in India, as restaurants redesign seating, menus, and service for guests of one.
food.nri_angle: The solo-dining wave mirrors what Indian buffet restaurants in the US already see, and it changes what NRIs visiting India can expect: the corner table is no longer the loneliest seat in the house.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Crispy Corn: How to Make the Restaurant-Style Spicy Snack at Home
food.excerpt: Golden, spice-dusted sweet corn kernels with a shattering crunch — here is how to nail the Indian restaurant starter at home, plus the details that keep it crisp.
food.image_caption: Crispy corn tossed in chaat masala and chilli. The Indo-Chinese starter is made by deep-frying cornflour-coated kernels at 175 to 180 degrees Celsius.
food.nri_angle: A beloved Indian restaurant starter that home cooks in the US can make with pantry spices and grocery-store corn; note that Indian cornflour is sold as white cornstarch in American stores.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Why Modak Became Lord Ganesha's Favourite Sweet, According to Mythology
food.excerpt: From a divine contest on Mount Kailash to the ritual offering of 21 modaks, the sweet's bond with the elephant-headed god runs through myth, wisdom and devotion.
food.image_caption: Modaks prepared for naivedyam. Devotees customarily offer 21 modaks to Lord Ganesha during Ganesh Chaturthi.
food.nri_angle: Indian-American families keep the modak tradition alive at Ganesh Chaturthi, using the sweet and its myth as a way to pass cultural memory to the next generation.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: From Nalli Nihari to Lotus Mithais: How Delhi Is Feeding the BRICS Summit
food.excerpt: The Taj Mahal, New Delhi spent months researching delegate preferences to build an 'India Friendship Menu' for the 18th BRICS Summit — and every delegate goes home with a recipe book.
food.image_caption: Gulab jamuns soaked in sugar syrup. Delhi's kitchens are feeding the BRICS summit with a menu running from nalli nihari to lotus mithais.
food.nri_angle: The summit's culinary showcase highlights how Indian regional cuisine is now presented as soft power to world leaders — a source of pride for the diaspora watching from abroad.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Mumbai's Lalbaugcha Raja Food Waste to Power Civic Hospitals During Ganeshotsav
food.excerpt: Under BMC's 'Prasad to Power' plan, 8–10 tonnes of wet waste from Mumbai's most famous Ganesh pandal will be converted into electricity for municipal hospitals across the 11-day festival.
food.image_caption: Mumbai's Lalbaugcha Raja Ganesh idol. Food waste collected during the festival will power civic hospitals.
food.nri_angle: The initiative pairs faith with sustainability at one of the diaspora's most-watched festivals, giving NRIs who follow Ganeshotsav from Mumbai's celebrations a tangible example of Indian cities linking devotion to environmental responsibility.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Microlot coffee: Inside India's limited-edition world of specialty brews
food.excerpt: From Tata Coffee's Nullore Estate at the Starbucks Reserve Roastery to yeast-washed lots from Ratnagiri, India's microlots — tiny, experimental, estate-separated batches — are winning global awards and selling out in small runs.
food.image_caption: Freshly roasted specialty coffee beans. India's microlot scene is bringing limited-edition brews from estates in Coorg and Chikmagalur to urban cafes.
food.nri_angle: Indian specialty coffees are increasingly available through online roasters and premium cafes abroad, giving diaspora drinkers a traceable, estate-level cup from Coorg and Chikmagalur.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: MasterChef's Jyoti Vishnani on Building an Indian Kitchen Under ₹10,000
food.excerpt: The MasterChef India Season 4 contestant says a great Indian kitchen comes down to ingredients, technique and wisely chosen tools — not expensive gadgets.
food.image_caption: Chef Jyoti Vishnani in her kitchen. The MasterChef contestant shares how to build an Indian kitchen for under ₹10,000.
food.nri_angle: NRIs setting up first kitchens abroad can build the same starter kit — pressure cooker, kadhai, tawa, masala dabba — for a fraction of a month's eating-out budget.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Which Roti Wins on Protein, Fibre, Iron and Calcium? Nutritionist's Answer
food.excerpt: Nutritionist Kiran Kukreja's comparison finds ragi leads on calcium, amaranth on protein and bajra on magnesium — but her real advice is to rotate grains, not abandon wheat.
food.image_caption: Rotis served with onion chutney. A nutritionist breaks down which roti wins on protein, fibre, iron and calcium.
food.nri_angle: Every one of these flours — ragi, jowar, bajra, makki, rajgira — is stocked in Indian grocery stores across the US and Canada, usually at prices close to wheat atta.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Atta Halwa: The Grainy, Ghee-Rich Whole-Wheat Dessert You Can Make in 25 Minutes
food.excerpt: A simple 1:1:1 ratio of flour, ghee and sugar — plus slow roasting and a warm syrup — delivers the danedar, juicy halwa of gurdwara fame, no lumps.
food.image_caption: A bowl of atta halwa garnished with slivered almonds. The grainy, ghee-rich whole-wheat dessert comes together in about 25 minutes.
food.nri_angle: Atta halwa uses only ingredients available in any American grocery store, making it one of the most practical Indian desserts for diaspora kitchens.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Lindt Opens Its First-Ever India Store in New Delhi's Aerocity
food.excerpt: The Swiss chocolatier's 1,100 sq ft Worldmark boutique features a 25-flavour LINDOR Pick & Mix bar, live chocolatiers and festive gifting ranges — a first for the brand in India.
food.image_caption: A flat-lay shows Lindt LINDOR truffles and a red gift box. Lindt & Söprüngli opened its first India store at Worldmark, Aerocity, New Delhi, on September 4.
food.nri_angle: A beloved international brand the diaspora grew up buying abroad is now a destination for visitors home — with a gifting angle timed for the Diwali season.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Air India Warns of Flight Disruptions as UK Air Traffic Fault Grounds 2,000 Flights
travel.excerpt: A technical failure at Britain's air traffic control provider NATS forced more than 1,750 flight cancellations on Tuesday, leaving over 330,000 passengers stranded. Air India advised travellers to check flight status before heading to the airport.
travel.image_caption: Delayed passengers queue with their luggage at Heathrow airport in west London on Tuesday. More than 1,750 flights were cancelled after a technical fault at Britain’s air traffic control provider NATS disrupted operations.
travel.nri_angle: Air India's UK routes connect London Heathrow and Birmingham with Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru — one of the busiest diaspora corridors — so the outage hits students, families and festive-season bookings directly; passengers should check flight status before heading to the airport and know their rebooking and duty-of-care rights under UK rules.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Twenty-Five Years After 9/11, U.S. Begins Rolling Back Travel Restrictions
travel.excerpt: From the end of the shoes-off rule to water bottles for PreCheck members and gate access at 13 airports, a quarter century after the attacks the U.S. is easing the checkpoint rituals that defined a generation of travel.
travel.image_caption: Travellers wait in a security line at a U.S. airport checkpoint. A quarter century after 9/11, the U.S. is easing some of the screening rules that reshaped air travel.
travel.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora — heavy long-haul flyers with Diwali travel weeks away — the shoe-rule rollback eases journeys for elderly parents, a water-bottle exception would help families with children, and gateside access restores the ritual of farewell at the gate.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Seven Weekend Getaways From Delhi You Can Reach by Bus
travel.excerpt: No flight, no car, no problem: Rishikesh, Jaipur, Agra, Mussoorie, Jim Corbett, Dehradun and Lansdowne are all within 290 km of Delhi and reachable by bus for a Friday-to-Sunday escape.
travel.image_caption: Rafts on the Ganga near Rishikesh, one of seven weekend getaways within bus range of Delhi. The destinations span adventure, heritage and wildlife escapes, all reachable without a flight or a car.
travel.nri_angle: NRIs visiting Delhi without a car can still manage a full weekend trip — regular intercity buses to all seven destinations make this list directly usable during a typical India visit.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Kolkata's Floating Hotel Has a Railway Track Running Through It
travel.excerpt: Polo Floatel Kolkata, India's only floating luxury hotel, has a working railway crossing on its grounds where trains pass within metres of guests — rooms run ₹4,000 to ₹6,000 a night.
travel.image_caption: A railway track runs through the landscaped grounds of the Polo Floatel Kolkata. The property is India's first and only floating luxury hotel, permanently moored on the Hooghly River.
travel.nri_angle: For diaspora travellers returning to Kolkata — especially around Durga Puja season — the Floatel offers an offbeat stay that turns a routine homecoming into a story, at mid-market prices.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: IRCTC Shatters Records as 20 Lakh Tickets Booked in a Single Day
travel.excerpt: The September 7 milestone marks the first time India's online railway ticketing platform has crossed the 20-lakh single-day mark, with upgraded servers and anti-bot measures keeping the system stable through the Diwali booking rush.
travel.image_caption: Second seating inside an Indian Railways coach. IRCTC set a record with over 20 lakh tickets booked in a single day.
travel.nri_angle: NRIs planning Diwali travel to India should book now: the 60-day advance reservation window concentrates festive demand, and Aadhaar verification is compulsory for individual users booking when the window opens.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: "Why Did You Lie?": Air India Crew Member Surprises Parents Onboard
travel.excerpt: Sushmita Nath told her parents she was on a different flight — then waited at the aircraft door. Her mother's first words, "Juth kyu boli?" (Why did you lie?), melted millions of hearts.
travel.image_caption: An Air India aircraft. An Air India crew member surprised her parents during a flight in an emotional reunion captured on video.
travel.nri_angle: The video resonates strongly with diaspora families, for whom reunions are rarer and an Air India uniform represents success that circles back to Indian roots.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Diwali Airfares Surge up to 340% on Some Regional Routes
travel.excerpt: One-way economy fares on select festive routes, from Kolkata-Deoghar to Delhi-Patna, have risen two to three times their usual levels as the Durga Puja and Diwali travel rush meets limited seat availability.
travel.image_caption: An Air India passenger aircraft descends for landing with its landing gear deployed. Domestic airfares on select festive routes in India have risen as much as 340% as the Durga Puja and Diwali travel rush fills available seats.
travel.nri_angle: Overseas Indians heading home for the festivals should budget for sharply higher domestic fares on onward legs to tier-2 and tier-3 cities.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Thailand Cuts Visa-Free Stay to 30 Days: What Indian Travellers Must Know
travel.excerpt: From September 15, Thailand replaces its 60-day visa exemption with a 30-day tourism-only category for 60 countries including India, with limits on land-border entries.
travel.image_caption: A graphic confirms Thailand's new 30-day and 15-day visa exemption rules. From September 15, Indian tourists get visa-free entry for up to 30 days, down from 60.
travel.nri_angle: Thailand is among the most popular short-haul leisure destinations for Indians; NRIs and resident Indians planning festive-season trips should confirm entry rules before booking.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: IndiGo Flight from Lucknow to Dammam Makes Emergency Landing in Ahmedabad After Bomb Note Found
travel.excerpt: All 107 passengers and six crew on flight 6E97 were deplaned safely; nothing suspicious was found after searches by police, CISF, and bomb disposal squads.
travel.nri_angle: The Lucknow-Dammam route is heavily used by Indian migrant workers in the Gulf, for whom such disruptions mean missed workdays and connecting-flight chaos.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Justice Department Sues Arkansas Over In-State Tuition for Immigrant Students
carousel.excerpt: Thursday's lawsuits against Arkansas, Hawaii, Utah and D.C. bring the administration's total to 25, as the DOJ says it has now challenged every state offering tuition breaks to noncitizens.
carousel.image_caption: The Arkansas State Capitol in Little Rock. The Justice Department has sued Arkansas, Hawaii, Utah and Washington, D.C., over laws granting in-state tuition to noncitizen students.
carousel.nri_angle: The outcome matters well beyond Arkansas: immigrant families across the 25 sued states — including Indian students and work-authorized families paying in-state rates — face the prospect of sharply higher college costs.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Indian-Origin Surrey Landlady Arrested After Tenant's Viral Harassment Videos
carousel.excerpt: Raj Tiwana was taken into custody by Surrey Police after a tenant documented alleged harassment, unauthorized entries, and physical confrontations in videos that spread widely online. Police have issued no official statement, and the exact charges remain unclear.
carousel.image_caption: Two Surrey Police officers escort a handcuffed woman outside a house in Surrey, British Columbia. The woman is Raj Tiwana, the Indian-origin landlady taken into custody after her tenant posted viral videos alleging harassment and unauthorized entry at the rental property.
carousel.nri_angle: An Indian-origin landlady's arrest in Canada shows diaspora landlords must follow provincial tenancy law, not personal confrontation, when disputes arise.

carousel.title: Keerthy Suresh Brings Contemporary Kanjivaram to TIFF 2026 Dorothy Premiere
carousel.excerpt: The actor walked the Toronto red carpet in a burgundy-and-gold Kanjivaram-inspired ensemble for the world premiere of her Tamil drama Dorothy, which earned a standing ovation in the festival's Centrepiece section.
carousel.image_caption: Keerthy Suresh poses on the red carpet at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival in a burgundy and antique-gold contemporary Kanjivaram-inspired ensemble. She attended the world premiere of her Tamil film Dorothy, directed by Karthik Subbaraj, which earned a standing ovation at the festival.
carousel.nri_angle: Toronto is home to one of North America's largest South Asian communities, and the Dorothy premiere gives diaspora audiences an early festival encounter with a Tamil film before its September 25 theatrical release.

carousel.title: Nepal Beat UAE to Win ACC Premier Cup and Book Asia Cup 2027 Spot
carousel.excerpt: Aasif Sheikh's century and Gulsan Jha's late assault powered Nepal to 313, before Karan KC and Lalit Rajbanshi derailed a UAE chase anchored by Rahul Chopra's unbeaten hundred at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur.
carousel.image_caption: Nepal's players celebrate with the trophy and a champions banner after winning the ACC Men's Premier Cup 2026 final. Nepal beat the UAE by 44 runs in Kuala Lumpur to seal qualification for the Asia Cup 2027.
carousel.nri_angle: The UAE's squad is stacked with Indian-origin players, including captain Harpreet Singh Bhatia and centurion Rahul Chopra, highlighting the diaspora's role in Gulf cricket.

carousel.title: MIT's Injectable 'Nanoantennas' Destroy Drug-Resistant Brain Cancer Cells
carousel.excerpt: The magnetically activated HITMAN technology eliminated 52 percent of chemotherapy-resistant glioblastoma cells in lab tests and extended survival in mice, without harming healthy brain tissue.
carousel.image_caption: An illustration of injectable nanoantennas being wirelessly activated by a magnetic field to target a brain tumor. MIT Media Lab researchers developed the HITMAN technology to destroy drug-resistant glioblastoma cells while leaving healthy tissue unharmed.
carousel.nri_angle: The breakthrough was led by MIT Media Lab's Deblina Sarkar, an Indian-origin researcher heading the Nano-Cybernetic Biotrek group.

carousel.title: Global Funds Lose Faith in India as Some Cut Stock Allocations to Zero
carousel.excerpt: Money managers at Janus Henderson and Vantage Point have pared India exposure to zero, and foreign portfolio ownership has tumbled to a 17-year low as AI-rich North Asia steals the flows.
carousel.image_caption: An illustration shows hands pulling apart the pieces of a red pie chart. Global funds have pulled a net $25 billion from Indian stocks this year, with foreign portfolio ownership of NSE-listed companies falling to a 17-year low.
carousel.nri_angle: India raised $127 billion from its diaspora to defend the rupee, showing how directly overseas Indians are being pulled into the country's currency battle — and NRI portfolios tied to Indian equities are feeling the foreign exodus first-hand.
